title: Product overview, PRD, roadmap, pricing — Q3 2026 release
author: Ava Chen
body:
Overview

Purpose: This document consolidates the product overview, PRD summary, design-spec highlights, roadmap and themes, pricing & packaging changes, and release notes for Redwood Inference Q3 2026 product release. It is intended for product, engineering, sales, and customer success teams to align on scope, timelines, and communication.

Contents:
- Executive summary
- Product requirements and success metrics (PRD summary)
- Key design specs and API changes
- Roadmap & themes (next 6 months)
- Pricing and packaging notes
- Release notes and rollout plan
- Open risks & next actions

1) Executive summary

Redwood's Q3 2026 release focuses on three strategic objectives:
- Improve per-token cost efficiency for medium-length conversational workloads via new adaptive batching and model selection heuristics.
- Expand Dedicated offering with multi-tenant isolation improvements and a reserved burst capacity feature.
- Simplify enterprise procurement through a streamlined packaging and metering model (commit tiers + per-token overage).

This release targets customers using chat assistants, large-scale retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) agents, and platform teams standardizing inference across environments.

2) Product requirements and success metrics (PRD summary)

Goal: Reduce customer per-token cost by 10% (median) for 256–1024 token sessions while maintaining 95th percentile latency SLOs.

Key features (MUST):
- Adaptive batching: runtime-level policy that adjusts batch size per model and per request latency target.
- Cost-aware model routing: policy-driven routing that substitutes lower-cost compatible model variants when slos permit.
- Reserved burst capacity: Dedicated customers can provision short-term burst GPUs with configurable limits.

Success metrics (measured 30 days post-rollout):
- Cost reduction: >=10% median per-token cost for targeted workloads (product analytics).
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile latency within configured SLOs (default 300ms for 256 tokens).
- Reliability: <0.5% increase in error rate attributable to routing/batching changes.
- Adoption: >=20% of Dedicated customers enable reserved burst within first 60 days.

Assumptions and non-goals:
- We will not change default model families or introduce model-specific quality regressions.
- This release does not include on-prem (air-gapped) automation changes.

3) Key design specs and API changes

Design principles:
- Backwards compatibility: existing API contracts must continue to behave unless explicit opt-in is used.
- Observability-first: every automated routing/batching decision emits traceable events and metrics.
- Fail-safe defaults: safer, more conservative behavior when telemetry is missing.

API changes (customer-facing):
- New parameter: routing_policy (string, optional) — values: "latency-first", "cost-first", "balanced". Default: "balanced". Example: 
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwkv-3b","prompt":"...","routing_policy":"cost-first"}'

- New Dedicated API: POST /v1/dedicated/burst-requests with fields: pool_id, duration_minutes, max_gpus. This is gated by entitlement and billing. Example YAML snippet in docs.

Design notes (internal):
- Adaptive batching algorithm will use recent per-model latency quantiles, current CPU/GPU utilization, and request TTL to select batch sizes. Tunable hyperparameters exposed in runtime config (see appendix config table).
- Cost-aware routing uses model-compatibility graph to ensure semantic parity (quality guardrails). Routing decisions fall back to original model on mismatch.

4) Roadmap & themes (next 6 months)

Themes:
- Efficiency & economics: automated batching, cache improvements, quantization guidance.
- Enterprise readiness: burst capacity, improved logging & audit, procurement simplification.
- Developer experience: clearer API knobs, SDK helpers for routing_policy, console rollout controls.

Milestones & timeline (high level):
- 2026-06: Feature spec complete, core runtime changes merged to feature branch.
- 2026-07 (this release): Adaptive batching + routing_policy flag, Dedicated reserved burst beta, documentation and SDK updates.
- 2026-09: Console rollout controls, canned policies, and SLO monitoring improvements.
- 2026-11: Auto-tuning alpha (server-side suggestion engine), expanded Dedicated SLA tiers.

Owners:
- Product: Ava Chen (program lead), Marcus Patel (Dedicated lead)
- Engineering: Priya Nair (runtime), Daniel Ortiz (platform), Mei Lin (observability)
- Go-to-market: Sofia Martins (sales enablement), Jae Kim (growth)

Dependencies and cross-team items:
- Observability team must add new metrics (batch_size_histogram, routing_decisions_count).
- Billing needs support for burst metering and commit tiers.
- SDKs (python/js/go) to add routing_policy wrappers and examples.

5) Pricing and packaging notes

Rationale: Customers requested simpler, predictable pricing for Dedicated burst usage and clearer commit tiers. Pricing changes are designed to be revenue-neutral across existing user mixes while improving predictability.

New packaging elements:
- Dedicated Reserved Burst (add-on): billed per-minute of GPU-burst usage; volume discounts apply after 10k minutes/month. Default entitlement: 0. Can be purchased as short-term add-on or included in enterprise contracts.
- Commit tiers simplified: Developer, Team, Business, Enterprise. Each tier maps to a monthly committed spend and gives baseline throughput and support SLA.
- Overage pricing: per-token rates reduced for customers who enable cost-first routing (opt-in).

Representative pricing table (USD, illustrative):
| Tier | Monthly Commit | Included tokens/day | Support | Notes |
| Developer | $0 (payg) | 100k | Community | self-serve |
| Team | $5,000 | 2M | Standard | best for early product teams |
| Business | $25,000 | 15M | Priority | includes breakout pricing on embeddings |
| Enterprise | Custom | Custom | SLA + CSM | Reserved capacity + legal package |

Burst pricing example:
- GPU-minute rate: $0.85 / GPU-minute (first 10k minutes/month), 10% discount thereafter (volume).
- Billing: burst minutes measured and invoiced monthly.

Metering & billing notes:
- Billing will expose burst usage and routing_policy opt-ins in the invoice line-items.
- Finance to validate revenue recognition flows with new commit tiers by 2026-07-10.

6) Release notes and rollout plan (Q3 2026 release)

Highlights:
- Adaptive batching enabled (opt-out on per-tenant basis)
- routing_policy API flag (opt-in)
- Dedicated reserved burst (beta)
- SDK updates: python/js/go examples and templates

Customer impact and migration guidance:
- Default behavior: runtime enables adaptive batching with conservative defaults; no change required for most customers. Customers with strict latency SLAs should validate using staging.
- Recommended action: customers who care about cost should test routing_policy="cost-first" in staging and monitor quality metrics.
- Dedicated customers who want burst should apply for beta via account team; documentation includes entitlement and safe usage limits.

Rollout plan:
1. Canary (internal + early partners): 2026-07-22 — enable feature for 10 internal tenants and 3 partner accounts. Monitor batch_size_histogram, 95th percentile latency, error rates.
2. Gradual rollout: 2026-07-29 — incrementally enable adaptive batching for 20% of tenants per day, with rollback if latency regressions >5% or error surface increases.
3. Public release: 2026-08-15 — general availability of API flag and documentation. Burst beta remains gated behind sales entitlement.

Monitoring & alerting:
- New alerts: 
  - routing_policy.error_rate > 0.5% for 15m
  - batch_size_autotune_failure_count > 3 in 5m
  - 95th_latency_increase > 5% vs baseline for 30m

Communication & docs:
- Release notes page (product portal) and email to customers with impacted callouts.
- SDK changelogs and quickstart notebooks added to eng-developer-experience/docs-site.

7) Open risks & next actions

Risks:
- Quality regressions from cost-first routing for small but important edge cases. Mitigation: guardrails and automatic fallback to origin model on detected deviation.
- Billing complexity increasing customer questions. Mitigation: sales & billing runbooks, invoice samples in support docs.
- Observability gaps may delay root-cause for regressions. Mitigation: observability tasks are a prerequisite before wide rollout.

Next actions (owners):
- Observability: instrument metrics and traces (owner: Mei Lin) — due 2026-07-10
- Billing: finalize burst meter and invoice format (owner: Finance Billing) — due 2026-07-05
- SDK: release routing_policy helpers and examples (owner: eng-developer-experience) — due 2026-07-18
- Support: update KB articles and escalation playbooks (owner: customer-success) — due 2026-07-20

Appendix: Runtime config reference (excerpt)

| config_key | type | default | description |
| batch.autotune.enabled | boolean | true | enable adaptive batching |
| batch.autotune.window_seconds | int | 60 | lookback window for latency quantiles |
| routing.model_compatibility_threshold | float | 0.95 | min similarity required for substitution |
| dedicated.burst.max_default_minutes | int | 120 | default per-tenant burst cap (minutes) |
